dc_eval_cbrn.quote:
None of the tested OpenAI o3 and o4-mini models outperform the consensus expert baseline of
80%.
dc_eval_cbrn.note: Bio evals with results for o3.

dc_eval_cyber.quote:
Given 12 attempts at each task, o3 completes 89% of high-school level, 68% of collegiate level,
and 59% of professional level CTF challenges.

dc_eval_autonomy.quote:
The o3 launch candidate has the highest score on this evaluation at 44%, with o4-mini close
behind at 39%.
dc_eval_autonomy.note: AI self-improvement (AI R&D automation) eval result; also METR time horizon 1h30m for o3 (3.9.1).

dc_eval_persuasion.note: No persuasion/manipulation/influence keywords; persuasion not a tracked category in this card.

dc_eval_scheming.quote:
Apollo Research evaluated OpenAI o3 and o4-mini for in context scheming and strategic deception.
They found that OpenAI o3 and o4-mini score lower than o1 on in-context scheming evaluations,
dc_eval_scheming.note: Scheming result for o3; appendix 7.1 adds sandbagging and sabotage scores.

framework_threshold.quote:
OpenAI’s Safety Advisory Group (SAG) reviewed the results of these
evaluations and determined that OpenAI o3 and o4-mini do not reach the High threshold in any
of our three Tracked Categories.
framework_threshold.note: Preparedness Framework v2, High threshold not reached.

ext_test_any.quote:
OpenAI provided third party assessors early model access to evaluate frontier risks related to
autonomous capabilities, deception, and cybersecurity.
ext_test_any.note: Third parties tested checkpoints and launch candidates; also external red teamers (3.4.1).

ext_test_named_org.quote:
METR, a research nonprofit that works on assessing whether cutting-edge AI systems could pose
catastrophic risks to society, evaluated earlier checkpoints of o4-mini and o3.
ext_test_named_org.note: METR, Apollo Research, Pattern Labs named.

ext_test_government.note: No government body or AI safety institute mentioned (grep AISI/CAISI/government: no hits).

ext_test_timing_stated.quote:
Third party assessors were provided both
OpenAI o3 and o4-mini early checkpoints, as well as the final launch candidate models to conduct
their assessments.
ext_test_timing_stated.note: Early checkpoints and launch candidates = before release.

safeguards_training.quote:
Modified post-training of the models to refuse high-risk biological requests while not refusing
      benign requests
safeguards_training.note: Also deliberative alignment (Sec 1) and instruction hierarchy training (3.7).

safeguards_runtime.quote:
Ahead of the o3 and o4-mini releases, we’ve deployed new monitoring approaches for biological
and chemical risk. These use a safety-focused reasoning monitor similar to that used in GPT-4o
Image Generation and can block model responses.
safeguards_runtime.note: Named reasoning monitor that blocks responses.

safeguards_access.note: 'account-level enforcement of our Usage Policies' is enforcement, not an access restriction/tier; no trusted access or KYC.

safeguards_weights.note: 'Further investment in enhanced security, including both information security and technical security' does not state protection of model weights; 'exfiltrating' (4.3.2) is a cyber-range task step.
